locked_story.headline: A drone with an onboard Raspberry Pi scans the tundra line by line for things that don't belong, tested on a 10-day deployment with Quinhagak Search and Rescue (arXiv 2611.27017, Binghamton University, Hampden-Sydney College, Nalaquq LLC, posted November 20th): fast enough to keep up with the camera, precise in one scene, but it missed most planted objects in the other
locked_story.note: Only in-window Alaska story this week where machine learning is the actual subject (four researchers called it a slow week). Primary source is the preprint itself. Archive overlap: 2026-07-24 'box-that-waits' covered Quinhagak's local drone pilots (127 days ago, outside the 30-day window, allowed); this film's subject is the onboard detector and its test numbers, and the thesis must stay distinct from 'local pilots over autonomy'. Back-to-back drone object class with 11-23 (delivery, Windracers ULTRA): the hero changes, no cargo drone, a quadcopter scanner over a mudflat, and the subject is the detector, not the aircraft. dedupe check FRESH.

rungs.note: 4 researchers (science/fisheries, energy/defense/UAS/business, rural/Native/health/gov, wildcard plus primary-source mining incl. NSF API, arXiv, Federal Register), 73 of 80 WebSearch calls used. All four called it a slow week for Alaska AI news.
